items_missed: No agenda statement. Opened with 'let me go ahead and start by gathering some general details from you' — a roadmap fragment with no 10-15 minute timeframe and no 'sound good?' confirmation.

Never offered or priced packing services, even though Christy spent ten minutes describing boxes she and her son are assembling themselves and directly asked 'how do we go about doing this?' Straight revenue miss.
Never asked about additional rooms (garage, storage unit, balcony), storage stops, or additional stops.
Never asked the moving-stressor question — and Christy volunteered her stressor unprompted (elevator reservation windows and crew arrival timing), so the opening was handed to him.
No Worries Damage Coverage never mentioned. 'Insurance' appeared only as one word inside the what's-included list; the $2,000 coverage and the 60c/lb baseline were never explained.
Meet Your Mover never mentioned. He described movers as 'background checked, vetted, highly trained' but never told her she'd get an email with her mover's photo and info.

On-Time Guarantee never mentioned. Christy spent roughly three minutes on arrival-time risk ('if they're late here then we are screwed on our time at the other end') and the guarantee was the exact answer to that fear.
Entire Save Your Ass prep speech absent — no prep-equals-shorter-move-equals-lower-bill framing, no consolidation examples, no take-a-carload tip, no sense-check close.
No booking attempt. He confirmed availability on Sept 18 in the first two minutes and never came back to it, even after she said she was collecting three quotes.
'No deposit required' never said — one of our two headline differentiators, and it was the natural counter to a shopping-three-quotes customer.
Never described the bolded detail list at the top of the confirmation email or asked her to reply with corrections to verify the info.
Business hours and how to reach us never given.
Never used Christy's name once after spelling it out — zero name use across a 28-minute call.
Specialty/awkward-item handling never addressed despite a six-foot boxed hutch, glass-topped stacked end tables, two reclining sofas and a treadmill.
Assembly/reassembly time never discussed even though an expandable table is in three separate boxes, both sofa backs come off, and there's a bed and standing desk.
No school-bus or other size equivalent used to sanity-check the load against the truck.
No Ecobox referral to a customer actively acquiring 20-25 boxes.
top_strength: The inventory intake was genuinely patient and it mattered. Christy had an unusual situation — most of her son's furniture is still boxed from the furniture store — and she was struggling to describe it ('I don't even know how you want me to tell you this'). Garrison gave her a clean framework instead of getting lost with her: 'anything that is boxed honestly, we could probably just count it as a box... unless it's incredibly large or awkward shaped, maybe call that out.' He also handled the unknown walk distance honestly rather than guessing silently, telling her 'I'll go ahead and assume we've got a little bit on the upper end of an average walk... once you've got details on that I can just plug it in.' And the pest-control aside ('I'm actually going through a pest control scenario right now at home... you gotta get multiple quotes') turned her three-quotes comment from an objection into a rapport moment.
coaching_note: LIVE BUSINESS RISK — estimate accuracy. He quoted 4.5-5.5 hours with two movers and one truck for what is effectively a full one-bedroom apartment load (about 25 furniture pieces including a 6-ft hutch, two reclining sofas, a treadmill, three area rugs, two dressers and a 65-inch console) plus 20-25 boxes, three steps at origin, a fourth-floor elevator with an unknown walk, and roughly an hour of drive each way. That is thin, and it is exactly the pattern in the bottom-4 review: underestimating apartments. Have him re-check this one in EMMA before the 18th. Second flag, lower confidence: the transcript records the high-end total as '$21,074' where the math is $218 x 5.5 + $75 = $1,274 — almost certainly a transcription artifact, but worth a listen to confirm she wasn't quoted a garbled number. Coaching-wise, the highest-leverage fix is Save Your Ass, and this call is the cleanest example of why: she was mid-packing, actively boxing her son's things, and asked him outright how to handle it. He should have said 'Christy, here's the single biggest thing you can do to keep this bill down — everything you consolidate before we get there is time we're not billing you for. Loose items in drawers, anything off the walls, the small stuff. And if anything fits in your car, take a carload the day before. Does that make sense?' That's ten points and it directly serves the estimate. Second priority: he had a customer whose one stated fear was arrival timing and he answered it with mover vetting instead of the On-Time Guarantee. 'If we miss that window, we start discounting immediately' would have closed her concern and probably the sale. Third: he never asked for the booking and never said no deposit — a shopping-three-quotes customer is precisely who needs both. And use her name.
phone_presence_notes: Consistently warm and patient through a confusing 15-minute inventory, with a real rapport moment on the pest-control quotes and genuine empathy on her elevator-timing worry ('I absolutely understand that') — held back from a 5 by zero use of her name and heavy verbatim filler ('absolutely, absolutely', 'got it, got it', 'perfect, perfect').
